mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together after a recent dip, weekday trip chaining returns and retail visits increase within four weeks. The mechanism predicts higher RETAIL_REC because commuting and errand bundling restore discretionary footfall.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days after a week in which WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase from the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RESIDENTIAL time below its recent level signals more out-of-home activity and less home-based substitution, which lifts retail recreation within one to two weeks. The effect should appear quickly if people are shifting from staying home to going out.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 7 after having been at or above 8 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops across the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated while RETAIL_REC stays depressed, routine essential trips spill into discretionary shopping on the same outing and retail recreation rises over the next four weeks. The mechanism depends on continuing convenience-trip traffic rather than a complete collapse in local activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a tightening mobility environment that suppresses discretionary retail demand within two weeks. Retail recreation should weaken further when commuting access and workplace attendance both contract together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after two consecutive weekly decreases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upswing in PARKS indicates weather- and season-driven outdoor substitution that diverts outings away from indoor retail recreation, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when park use is already far below baseline and then rebounds.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points from the prior week after being below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days after PARKS rebounds from below -40 by at least 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stops falling and turns upward, access friction to shopping districts eases and retail recreation improves within one week. This is a short-lag accessibility channel: more transit use should precede more retail visits, not the reverse.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases week-on-week after being negative for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after TRANSIT turns up from a two-week negative streak.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL and rise in WORKPLACES indicates normalization of outside-the-home routines, which should lift retail recreation over the next two to four weeks. The hypothesis fails if people leave home more for work but do not convert that movement into discretionary retail stops.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its recent 4-week average despite RESIDENTIAL declining and WORKPLACES rising together.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both strengthen while PARKS remains weak, the area is shifting toward routine utilitarian trips rather than leisure substitution, which should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The retail channel fails when outdoor leisure rebounds strongly enough to offset the utilitarian pattern.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES remain above baseline and PARKS stays far below baseline.
